source.title_on_document: POET: Supporting Prompting Creativity and Personalization with Automated Expansion of Text-to-Image Generation

paper_design_summary: The paper evaluates POET, a text-to-image tool that identifies and expands homogeneous dimensions of model outputs, using an automatic model evaluation and a within-subjects user study. The automatic evaluation samples 1,000 Flickr30K prompts and generates 10 images for each selected prompt using baseline models and POET variants, scoring within-prompt image variation with ICAD (PDF pp. 7-8, Section 4). In the 28-person study recruited from US college campuses, participants rated pre-generated image-pair differences, then prompted Base versus POET and personalized versions of each; outcomes were perceived image difference, prompting rounds until satisfaction, and self-rated satisfaction (PDF pp. 8-12, Section 5).

ai_tool.name_model: Flux.1-dev Base and POET variants; homogeneous-dimension identification by prompt inversion, BLIP-2+LLaMA-7b, LLaVA-1.5-7b, or GPT-4o; additional GPT-4o image generation with GPT-Image-1 backend
ai_tool.how_used: Models generate images from sampled dataset prompts without creative-task participants. The identification-strategy comparison replaces only that component of POET; the expansion ablation omits homogeneous-dimension identification (PDF p. 7, Sections 4.1-4.2).

task.description: Generate image sets from Flickr30K captions and compare within-prompt visual variation across baseline and POET configurations (PDF pp. 7-8, Sections 4.1-4.2). Consistency with the original prompt is illustrated qualitatively in Section 4.2.3 and Figure 7, without a separate scored consistency outcome.

outcomes.name: Intra-Class Average Distance (ICAD) of images generated from the same prompt
outcomes.question: none
outcomes.measure_detail: ICAD quantifies average pairwise diversity among images generated from the same prompt; its stated range is 0 to 1, with higher values indicating more visual variation (PDF p. 7, Section 4.2.2). This is variation within model-generated image sets, not diversity across human creators. Unit=set denotes the images generated for one sampled prompt in a model configuration; n_units=1,000 is the sampled-prompt count, not a count of people, pairs, or pooled observations across configurations (Section 4.1). Table 1's identification strategies and Figures 4-5's model/expansion comparisons are variants of this outcome. The PDF does not specify the ICAD feature extractor or report SDs, SEs, confidence intervals, or a statistical test for these scores; statistics_available=none records the absence of those statistics. The printed POET values differ across displays: 0.482 in Table 1, 0.48 in the text accompanying Figure 4, and 0.481 in the text accompanying Figure 5; each is retained with its own locator.

eligibility.reason: The user study analyzes 28 people in total, below 50 (PDF p. 2, Abstract; p. 15, Conclusions; p. 12, Tables 4-5). It compares AI configurations within participants with counterbalanced order; random assignment of people or condition order is not stated (PDF pp. 8-9, Sections 5 and 5.1.1-5.1.2). No outcome scores creativity or cross-person diversity of participants' own outputs: Phase 1 rates supplied model-generated image pairs, while Phases 2 and 3 report prompting rounds and self-rated satisfaction (PDF pp. 8-12, Sections 5.1-5.3 and Tables 3-5). The statement 'every scenario was seen by 6 participants' (PDF p. 9, Section 5.1.2), across four scenarios, implies 24 people (6 x 4), conflicting with the reported total of 28; the paper does not explain this discrepancy. The separate Flickr30K evaluation is model-only: 1,000 sampled prompts and their generated images do not count as people, and ICAD compares images from the same prompt rather than different human creators (PDF pp. 7-8, Sections 4.1-4.2). Neither study supplies AI-versus-human output comparisons or eligible observational creativity/diversity evidence; context_class remains none.

one_line_finding: With 28 participants, POET image pairs were rated more different than Base pairs in the fictional-character reference scenario (2.28 points on a 7-point scale, SE 0.203, Table 3, PDF p. 12), and POET reached satisfaction in 0.857 fewer rounds (SE 0.453, p < .1) with 0.600 higher self-rated satisfaction (SE 0.229) in Phase 2 (Table 4, PDF p. 12).
